title: India Targets One Billion 5G Users by 2030 as Scindia Opens IMC 2026
excerpt: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia told the 10th India Mobile Congress that India has 550 million 5G users — the fastest adoption anywhere in the world — and set a goal of one billion by 2030, alongside a resolve to lead the world on 6G.
body:
• Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia set a target of one billion 5G users by 2030, up from 550 million today, speaking at the inauguration of the 10th India Mobile Congress (IMC) in New Delhi on Thursday.
  • India's 5G rollout now reaches 99.9% of districts and 86% of the population, with about ₹4.5 lakh crore invested and nearly 500,000 towers deployed in two-and-a-half years — the fastest 5G expansion anywhere in the world, according to the minister.
  • On 6G, the Bharat 6G Alliance — 90 institutions — has produced 7,700 patents, 4,400 of them international. India will also set up its first Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.
  • What it means for you: mobile data rates have fallen 97% in a decade, giving India some of the world's cheapest data. Near-universal 5G by 2030 means faster, affordable high-speed connectivity across nearly every district — and Prime Minister Modi used the same stage to push for a global framework to curb digital frauds, which could eventually mean stronger protections against scam calls.

India aims to nearly double its 5G user base from 550 million to one billion by 2030, Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said on Thursday, as he inaugurated the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi. "Today we have 550 million users on 5G... But we will not rest here. By 2030 our target is to take that number from 550 million to a billion customers on 5G," he said.

Context & Background

The announcement came at the inauguration of IMC 2026, Asia's largest digital technology event, held from October 7 to 10 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi under the theme "Scale Without Boundaries." Prime Minister Narendra Modi formally inaugurated the tenth edition on Thursday.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2108073049119711530

Scindia framed the target as the latest chapter in a remarkable turnaround. "We were behind the world in 4G. We marched with the world on 5G. But it is our resolve that we will lead the world on 6G," he said. According to PTI, the minister noted that India has invested around ₹4.5 lakh crore in rolling out 5G infrastructure, with nearly 500,000 telecom towers deployed in a record two-and-a-half years.

The minister also announced that India's first Telecom Manufacturing Zone will be established in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh — a dedicated ecosystem for telecom equipment, semiconductor companies and data centres aimed at strengthening domestic manufacturing.

Impact & Analysis

The numbers behind the announcement are striking. India now has 1.35 billion mobile subscribers, with broadband connections growing from 60 million people in 2014 to over 1 billion, and internet connectivity rising from 250 million to close to 1.2 billion. Mobile internet rates have dropped 97% over the past decade.

Scindia tied the expansion to the wider digital economy, arguing that 5G is important not just for telecom but for connecting machines, intelligence and transactions. "The mobile phone has become the new bank branch. The telecom connectivity network today has become the digital highway, and data today has become the fuel of the AI economy," he said at the Kautilya Economic Conclave earlier this week.

The digital-payments layer shows what connectivity unlocks: UPI, which started with 21 banks and 90,000 transactions a month, now has more than 740 banks live and processed 21,500 crore transactions in FY25-26, worth $3.4 trillion. The India AI Mission, with a corpus of nearly ₹10,000 crore, is assembling 38,000 GPUs, 14 cloud partners and over 250 AI models — a bet that telecom networks plus computing and AI will expand digital opportunity nationwide.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora — disproportionately represented in global telecom, software and AI workforces — the announcements are both a career and an investment signal. A billion-person 5G base and a domestic manufacturing ecosystem in Gwalior create new markets for equipment makers, cloud providers and AI startups, many of which already employ large India-based teams. And Modi's parallel call for a global anti-fraud framework speaks to a pain point diaspora families know well: scam calls that cross borders. "A person sitting in one country, with the help of a person in another country, can commit a crime in a third country," the Prime Minister said, urging the GSMA and global telcos to build mechanisms that stop fraud before it reaches people.

What's Next

IMC 2026 runs through October 10, with industry players and policymakers hashing out the path to the 2030 target. On 6G, India is participating in the standard-setting frameworks of the ITU and 3GPP, and the Bharat 6G Alliance is working through seven specialised groups covering spectrum, devices, applications and use cases. The next milestones to watch: the Gwalior Telecom Manufacturing Zone's build-out, India's share of global 6G patents, and whether the 550-million-to-one-billion trajectory holds as 4G users continue migrating to 5G networks.

"We were behind the world in 4G. We marched with the world on 5G. But it is our resolve that we will lead the world on 6G."

— Jyotiraditya Scindia, Union Minister for Communications
